- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — apply a dampening factor (e.g., 0.85–0.90 multiplier) to subsequent forecasts.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon — adjust downward by 1–3% for the last 5–10 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if price is above 85–90, forecast should trend downward; if below 80, forecast should trend upward — apply a smoothing filter to avoid sharp reversals.
- Forecast lag: model often predicts 1–2 days too early — shift forecast values forward by 1–2 days for the next 30-day window.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices — if last 5 days are above 88, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overestimating downward momentum.
